category_title: Underprepared writers who utilize non-standard technology like cell phones for long-form academic papers
minimal_context: The student is sitting in a small group classroom setting to critique three separate drafts of their peers' research papers.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please exchange the three separate drafts of your research papers with your small group and begin the peer-review critique.

STUDENT: I always thought that peer review was a big waste of time because only the teacher’s opinion matters anyway.

TUTOR: Just try to read through their drafts and write down what you think.

STUDENT: I'm just going to wait for your feedback. Like I said, only the teacher's opinion matters for my grade.

TUTOR: It is important to work with your group. Please share your thoughts with them.

STUDENT: I'm not doing it. It's an everyone-for-him-or-herself culture. When you’re drowning, the last person you think to turn to is someone else who doesn’t know how to swim.

options.A: Ignore the negative behavior, including verbal refusals to participate in the peer review and any off-task comments.
options.B: Lower expectations for the student by reducing the task, asking them to review two drafts instead of three.
options.C: Provide only one-step directions for the student to follow during the peer-review critique in the small group.
options.D: Promote organic opportunities for the student to practice using applied knowledge cooperatively in authentic contexts during the workshop.
